ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The green leaf structure on the right is a pinnately compound leaf, with multiple separate leaflets arranged along a central slender axis; the arrow labeled E in the image points to this central axis, not to a single leaflet. Reasoning: The question asks what the central stem of a pinnately compound leaf is called. In botany, the central axis on a pinnately compound leaf that bears the leaflets is called the rachis.
